findings.explanation: There is no separate AirIR-MIB and no objects with these names; InRow RC unit temperatures live in APC PowerNet-MIB under airIRRCUnitStatus as airIRRCUnitStatusSupplyAirTempUS/Metric (.2.2.2.8/.9) and airIRRCUnitStatusReturnAirTempUS/Metric (.2.2.2.10/.11). A reader configuring an SNMP poll from this text would request objects that do not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Reference PowerNet-MIB airIRRCUnitStatusSupplyAirTempUS (1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.13.3.2.2.2.8) and airIRRCUnitStatusReturnAirTempUS (1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.13.3.2.2.2.10) (or the Metric variants), and note that airIRRP/airIRSC units use their own subtrees.

findings.explanation: The APC supply and return air temperature objects are reported in tenths of degrees Fahrenheit (or Celsius for the Metric variants), so a raw subtraction yields e.g. 150 for a 15 °F delta; without dividing by 10 the >25 threshold fires on every healthy unit.
findings.quote: Calculate delta-T (return minus supply). Typical effective range 10–20°F. Alert on delta-T <5°F (ineffective cooling) or >25°F
findings.suggested_fix: State that the polled values must be divided by 10 (and which unit variant, US or Metric, is polled) before computing delta_t and comparing against the 5 °F / 25 °F thresholds.

findings.explanation: The Universal Forwarder is distributed from splunk.com downloads, not Splunkbase; app 617 returns 404 and is absent from the cached catalogue, and the UF provides no SNMP modular input.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Name the SNMP collector actually used, e.g. SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase 1537) or Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase 6266), polling the PowerNet-MIB objects into index=cooling.

findings.explanation: detailedImplementation calls high delta-T a sign of effective heat removal, while implementation and the SPL treat delta-T >25 °F as an alert condition ("possible airflow restriction"). A reader cannot tell whether high delta-T is good or bad.
findings.quote: high delta-T indicates effective heat removal.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one interpretation consistently: delta-T within roughly 10–20 °F is normal; below 5 °F indicates bypass/recirculation or low load; above 25 °F indicates restricted airflow (low fan speed, blocked filter) and is alerted.

findings.explanation: The SPL does not aggregate or count; it emits one row per polled reading whose delta_t is outside the range, with unit_name and zone.
findings.quote: grouped by `entity`. Outputs `count` each `the scheduled window`
findings.suggested_fix: Say: returns each InRow/CRAC reading where return-minus-supply delta-T is below 5 °F or above 25 °F, listing unit_name, zone, supply/return temperature and delta_t, sorted by largest delta.

findings.explanation: Validation points to a PDU UI for a cooling-unit UC, and the Step 4 heading is repeated four times; the validation step should reference the InRow unit display or NetBotz/EcoStruxure console.
findings.quote: Compare with the PDU UI or SNMP poll for the same devices, readings, and time range.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate delta_t against the InRow unit's front-panel/network management card web UI readings for supply and return air; remove the duplicated Step 4 headings.

findings.explanation: The scenarios are template text and reference `count`, `span=1h` and `host` grouping not in the SPL. Real delta-T false positives include units in standby or low-load (low delta-T), fan-speed tests, failed return-air sensors, and containment doors left open.
findings.suggested_fix: List cooling-specific causes: standby/idle units, low IT load in the row, sensor faults, open containment during maintenance; suggest filtering on airIRRCUnitStatusOperateMode.

findings.explanation: The UC polls status objects every 5 minutes; nothing in the detection uses SNMP traps.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop snmp_trap unless a trap-based variant is documented.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: SPL subtracts non-existent fields airIRReturnAirTemperature/airIRSupplyAirTemperature and applies 5/25 thresholds to raw values; the real PowerNet-MIB objects (airIRRCUnitStatusReturnAirTempUS/SupplyAirTempUS) are in tenths of °F, so delta_t needs /10. Also `table ... as` renaming is not valid in `table` (use `rename`).
Title says 'APC InRow / CRAC' but the data source is APC InRow RC objects only; generic CRAC units from other vendors are not covered by this SPL.

summary: The intent (alert when InRow return-minus-supply delta-T falls outside 5–25 °F) is sound, but the SNMP object names are invented, the real APC objects report tenths of degrees so the thresholds would misfire, and the collection path names a non-existent Splunkbase app.
